The Great Pyramid keeps attracting new theories. The research group Land of Chem brings Danny Jones one of the newest. It holds that the pyramid's chambers served as chemical production equipment in the ancient world. The guests present what they call evidence for ancient chemical factories inside the most studied building on earth.

Jones works through their readings of the chambers, shafts, and residues with them. The theory joins a crowded shelf of claims about the pyramid's purpose, nearly all rejected by Egyptologists, who hold to the tomb account. What this episode offers is the claimants' own tour of their evidence. Listeners interested in alternative Egyptology get the case in detail, and can measure it against the standard account for themselves.

Cliff Geppart tells Danny Jones how he built Conservative Grounds, a right-leaning coffee shop. Geppart calls it the first such shop in America. The idea grew after officers were asked to leave another cafe.

He and a friend vowed to open a place where no one gets thrown out. They filed papers in a month and signed a lease soon after. The shop took about five months to finish. Jones asks about politics served with coffee. The episode shows culture-war business at ground level, one cup at a time. The welcome-all claim anchors his whole pitch.
